review_text_raw:
Having played "A Normal Lost Phone", the concept of Simulacra isn't anything new to me, however due to this not being a particularly common way of making a game it is a welcome addition to this genre of sorts. 
Simulacra also comes with a couple of different twists compared to what "A Normal Lost Phone" had so it's not complete copy.

The good:
*You are thrown into an interesting story that you have to go through with the help of strangers. Who should you trust? Who should you be weary of? Wel that's the beauty, you don't know and you have to base your judgements on scraps of information that you can find. The story is definitely one of the highlights of this game.
*The gameplay whilst isn't groundbreaking works well for this game and doesn't propose any friction for the player on how to proceed.
*There's a decent bit of replayability in this game if you want to uncover all of the different paths. They also aren't particularly difficult to reach if given enough thought.

The bad:
*The horror elements of this game... Don't get me wrong, I love myself some horror and this game seems like a good candidate for a bit of it, however the way it is implemented in this specific game is forced and cliche.
Build tension through uneasiness, not through awful jumpscares.
*I don't need to be redirected to a webpage with a Discord server every time I finish the game. It is annoying. If I want to join your Discord Ill find a way to do it without it being showed in my face every time.
*For a game with so many branching I feel like it should've had a save system. If you want to get a specific achievement you are forced to replay the whole game. It is remedied by the faster conversations, but I do not want to listen to the same conversation for 7 times just so I can get an achievement.
*The acting leaves some things to be desired. I understand that this is an indie game but the video segments in this game felt somewhat robotic and lifeless.

Overall, Simulacra is a fun and interesting little game, that will not burn a hole in your wallet and will keep you entertained for a day or two. I think its worth giving a try, if you can stand the occasional jumpscare.

review_text_raw:
I got this game today and I was incredibly excited to play. I did around 4 playthroughs, trying to see the easter eggs and gather all the achievements and overall I'm rather amazed.

The use of real people in a game was a new concept to me but I enjoyed the idea a lot, especially since it highlighted the possible dangers of the digital world and made them more transferrable to the real world. The voice acting was a bit unrealistic sometimes but that's a minor issue. 

There are 5 possible endings (though the game at the end shows you only four of them) and your choices really impact them. The dialogue options that the game revolves around either make or break your case, so you have to think about what to choose.

The game is rather easy, in most cases if you get stuck at anything either of the two characters that you keep talking to will help you. 

After over 6 hours of playthrough, I have to say I am really impressed with this game. It was my first time ever playing something of this format and I will now have expectations for the future. I would not count this game as a horror, since the repeated jumpscares and glitches were far from scary (but maybe they might scare some people, who knows!). The true scary theme in the game is the realization that people on the Internet might really be bad and you shouldn't trust everyone you meet online. 

Even though it's common knowledge, when showcased like this, it can be eye-opening to some. Great game.

review_text_raw:
TLDR: Cute little horror game with lots of jump scares and some bad acting. Social media in this game was amazing fun. Pick it up on sale.

An adventure horror game all happening in somebody's phone. You essentially play as yourself, trying to solve the mystery of the phone's owner's disappearance with the help of her friends. The puzzles are not very difficult, but engaging enough to keep you hooked in the story. There were some really spooky segments so I'd recommend playing this in a dark quiet room to get its full potential.

The story was fun, reasonably short. Editing Anna's social media was definitely the biggest highlight of my playthrough - you get absolute freedom in Anna's phone. Devs could only make this better by adding more consequences to it. You will spend a lot of time talking to 2 of the biggest cringelords in games everywhere. Their strange behavior was topped off by their atrocious acting. Female acting was alright. There are multiple endings to reflect your choices.

All in all, I recommend getting this one on sale. It's not the best or most memorable game ever, but it's still fairly entertaining..

review_text_raw:
Wow. That was really cool, I finished it in one sitting. If you don't expect a polished masterpiece you will find a unique little gem in the rough.
It had moments that creeped me out, but the horror elements are on the mild side. The highlight (and main focus) of this game is the character conversations you have and the storytelling around that, especially in the context of being a detective on someone else's phone and them getting pulled into the investigation process. I really loved the combination of elements to it...
